title: Treat erectile dysfunction with an effective oral PDE5 inhibitor

concept.text: Enable erections sufficient for sexual activity through an oral medicine, replacing more invasive treatment for many patients. This is symptomatic treatment; it does not establish restoration of untreated erectile function. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for adult ED based on placebo-controlled clinical trials demonstrating improved erection attainment and maintenance on validated questionnaires and intercourse outcomes. Test set by: FDA; the sildenafil approval and prescribing information specify the indication and clinical evidence. Reported achieved: FDA approved sildenafil (Viagra) on 27 March 1998. Sources given: [Original FDA Viagra approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/1998/20895ltr.pdf) ; [FDA Viagra prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/020895s048lbl.pdf).

page.title: Oral PDE5 inhibition for erectile dysfunction
page.definition: An oral medicine inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), an enzyme that breaks down a signal relaxing penile erectile tissue, and improves the ability to obtain and maintain erections sufficient for intercourse during sexual stimulation. This treats erectile dysfunction during medicine use.

goal.need: Among Massachusetts men aged 40–69 without erectile dysfunction at baseline, 25.9 new cases occurred per 1,000 person-years. A tablet gives men an alternative to a vacuum device, penile injection, urethral medication or implant. In trials with diaries from about 1,600 men, about 66% of intercourse attempts succeeded with sildenafil, compared with 20% with placebo. The treatment requires sexual stimulation. Men taking nitrates cannot use it because the combination can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure.

figures.caption: Incidence of erectile dysfunction by age at study entry
figures.note: The analysis included 847 Massachusetts men without erectile dysfunction at baseline; these are incidence rates, not prevalence estimates.

statements.body: Pfizer Central Research, with Southmead Hospital
statements.quote: To determine the efficacy and safety of sildenafil
statements.context: The published objective concerned oral sildenafil in men with erectile dysfunction of no established organic cause.

statements.body: National Institutes of Health Consensus Development Conference on Impotence
statements.quote: Development of new therapies, including pharmacologic agents, and with emphasis on oral agents
statements.context: The panel gave priority to oral agents for erectile dysfunction without specifying a molecular target. The European Patent Office reproduced the recommendation in decision T 1212/01, section 5.13.

completion.title: FDA approves an oral PDE5 inhibitor for the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
completion.criterion: FDA approval takes effect for at least one new drug application whose approved prescribing information specifies oral administration, inhibition of phosphodiesterase type 5 and an indication for the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.105(a) and (c), and the approved prescribing information for the drug.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA will approve an application after it determines that the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling
completion.basis: FDA approved NDA 20-895 for oral sildenafil on March 27, 1998. The approved indication covers treatment during use. FDA exercised the same approval authority for tadalafil, whose principal as-needed trials used the erectile-function domain score and two Sexual Encounter Profile diary questions.

milestones.title: A PDE5 inhibitor's laboratory results support reasonably safe human testing for erectile dysfunction.
milestones.criterion: Animal or in vitro pharmacology and toxicology studies of an oral PDE5 inhibitor support the sponsor's conclusion that the proposed clinical investigations are reasonably safe, and an investigational new drug application for it is in effect at FDA, which permits clinical investigation in the United States. Evidence of enzyme selectivity alone, or an effective application with no report of the supporting studies, is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the general preclinical requirement for investigational drugs
milestones.threshold_quote: on the basis of which the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: A controlled patient study shows preliminary erectile benefit from an oral PDE5 inhibitor.
milestones.criterion: A controlled clinical study in men with erectile dysfunction shows an improvement in erectile response with the oral inhibitor relative to the control and assesses common short-term adverse effects. Erectile response may be measured during stimulation by an instrument or recorded by patients during treatment.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c).
milestones.threshold_quote: after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: Expanded trials establish erectile benefit and characterize risks sufficiently for prescribing information.
milestones.criterion: Expanded clinical studies in men with erectile dysfunction demonstrate that oral treatment improves the ability to achieve and maintain an erection sufficient for intercourse. Patient-reported erectile function or intercourse outcomes and the observed adverse reactions provide enough information to evaluate overall benefit and risk and to support physician labelling.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c), with clinical outcomes illustrated in the approved prescribing information for sildenafil and tadalafil.
milestones.threshold_quote: to evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug and to provide an adequate basis for physician labeling.

milestones.title: A PDE5 inhibitor enhances electrically evoked relaxation of isolated human erectile tissue.
milestones.criterion: Precontract strips of human corpus cavernosum and measure relaxation during electrical field stimulation under matched conditions with and without the inhibitor. The inhibitor increases the evoked relaxation relative to the drug-free response.
milestones.set_by: Human corpus cavernosum tissue-bath assay used by Rajfer and colleagues and subsequently by Ballard and colleagues for sildenafil.
milestones.threshold_quote: Relaxation responses resulting from electrical field stimulation (EFS) were then determined in the presence and absence of sildenafil.

milestones.title: Human studies establish oral dosing and tolerability sufficiently to design a controlled patient trial.
milestones.criterion: Initial studies in volunteers or patients characterize the candidate’s pharmacokinetics, pharmacologic effects and adverse effects with increasing oral doses sufficiently to design a well-controlled phase 2 study in men with erectile dysfunction.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies

milestones.title: FDA accepts an oral PDE5 inhibitor application for substantive review for erectile dysfunction.
milestones.criterion: FDA files a new drug application seeking the erectile dysfunction indication for an oral PDE5 inhibitor after determining that the application is sufficiently complete for substantive review.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

not_found: No PDE5-specific numerical preclinical pass threshold was found in the FDA regulations, approval letter or prescribing information.
The 1998 FDA joint clinical review had no readable text; its individual preclinical study results and cohort sizes could not be verified.
The full original 1992 NIH conference statement could not be verified directly.
No urological society or consensus panel statement disputing the general goal of effective oral PDE5 treatment was found.

results.finding: Viagra (sildenafil citrate), one IND, became effective on January 8, 1995.
results.quote:
FDA has verified the applicant's claim that the date 
the investigational new drug application became effective was on 
January 8, 1995.

results.finding: Viagra, one NDA, was initially submitted on September 29, 1997.
Sildenafil enhanced nitric oxide action in isolated human corpus cavernosum. Tissue sample size and effect magnitude were unreported.
results.quote:
Sildenafil has no direct
relaxant effect on isolated human corpus cavernosum, but enhances the effect of nitric oxide (NO)
by inhibiting phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), which is responsible for degradation of cGMP in
the corpus cavernosum.

results.finding: Rat fertility was unaffected by sildenafil at doses up to 60 mg/kg/day. Group sizes were unreported.
results.quote:
There was no impairment of fertility in rats given sildenafil up to 60 mg/kg/day for 36 days to
females and 102 days to males, a dose producing an AUC value of more than 25 times the human
male AUC.

results.finding: Healthy volunteers had more frequent adverse events with higher single oral sildenafil doses, studied up to 800 mg. Sample size was unreported.
results.quote:
In studies with healthy volunteers of single doses up to 800 mg, adverse events were similar to
those seen at lower doses but incidence rates were increased.

results.finding: Sildenafil improved stimulated erections versus placebo in 8 crossover studies of patients with erectile dysfunction. Patient count was unreported.
results.quote:
sexual stimulation
resulted in improved erections, as assessed by an objective measurement of hardness and duration
of erections (RigiScan®), after VIAGRA administration compared with placebo.

results.finding: In diary studies involving about 1,600 men with erectile dysfunction, sildenafil increased intercourse success by about 46 percentage points versus placebo.
results.detail: The 46-point difference is calculated from the label’s approximate group rates.
results.quote:
group mean success rates (total successes
divided by total attempts) were about 66% on VIAGRA vs about 20% on placebo.

results.finding: FDA-approved Viagra is an oral PDE5 inhibitor indicated for erectile dysfunction. Sample size is inapplicable.
results.detail: The label records market approval without specifying the NDA number or effective date.
results.quote:
VIAGRA®, an oral therapy for erectile dysfunction, is the citrate salt of sildenafil, a selective
inhibitor of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-specific phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5).

results.finding: In isolated human corpus cavernosum strips (n unreported), sildenafil increased electrically evoked relaxation to 3 times the drug-free response.
results.quote: Sildenafil (0.001 to 1 microM) enhanced the EFS-induced, nitric oxide (NO) dependent, relaxation of HCC in a concentration-dependent manner to a maximum of 3 times the pretreatment level at 1 microM sildenafil.

results.finding: Oral avanafil had a no-observed-adverse-effect level of 10 mg/kg/day in 32 male beagles. FDA records that clinical trials proceeded under the IND.
results.detail: The dog study used daily oral capsules. FDA’s retrospective NDA review documents that trials proceeded under the IND and that FDA reviewed the supporting nonclinical data under it.
results.quote:
Clinical trials were conducted and supporting nonclinical data were reviewed under IND 
51,235.

results.finding: One avanafil tablet NDA (202276) reached substantive FDA review, as reflected in correspondence citing the September 1, 2011, Filing Communications Letter.
results.detail: FDA gave August 28, 2011, as a prospective filing date contingent on sufficient completeness. The supplied portion of the filing correspondence describes preliminary review issues, and later correspondence documents ongoing review.
results.quote:
We also refer to our September 1, 2011, Filing Communications Letter, in which we notified you 
of our target date of March 11, 2012, for communicating labeling changes and/or postmarketing 
requirements/commitments in accordance with the “PDUFA REAUTHORIZATION 
PERFORMANCE GOALS AND PROCEDURES – FISCAL YEARS 2008 THROUGH 2012.”
